paragraph: In October 2026 [President Lourenço said the National Cloud and Government Data Center were built to secure public administration systems](<https://pti.ao/estado-da-nacao-presidente-destaca-progressos-nas-telecomunicacoes-e-transformacao-digital/>). In the last twelve months, [President Lourenço opened the National Data Centre and Cloud at Camama on 28 April 2026](<https://www.menosfios.com/data-centers-em-angola-quais-tem-certificacao-internacional/>). At the opening the telecoms ministry said the [government cloud is expected to keep information within national borders](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/2904-55113-angola-launches-national-data-center-to-support-digital-strategy>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

[Iwacu reports](<https://www.iwacu-burundi.org/lia-au-coeur-de-la-strategie-numerique-au-burundi/>) that Burundi's national AI strategy was validated at a workshop in April 2026. The strategy provides for modernising the Setic data center and developing a sovereign cloud. In the last twelve months, [the strategy validated on 22 April 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/burundi-une-strategie-nationale-de-l-ia-adossee-a-six-piliers>) is the step found: it pairs sovereign cloud solutions with data centre modernisation. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

[Decree 2026-579 of 2 September 2026](<https://www.lanation.bj/actualites/presidence-de-la-republique-un-comite-national-du-numerique-cree>) created a National Digital Committee under the President, with protection of strategic data among its priorities. In the last twelve months, [Benin's digital agency ASIN proposed in June 2026 a governance framework](<https://www.lanation.bj/actualites/usages-de-lia-dans-ladministration-publique-un-cadre-de-gouvernance-envisage>) for generative-AI use in public administration. It calls for sovereign hosting and contractual reversibility. In October 2026 an official [said Beninese data stays in Benin](<https://transcontinents.africa/fr/article/e-gouvernance-le-benin-et-la-mauritanie-a-lecole-estonienne>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

In January 2026 Burkina Faso's Prime Minister [ordered all state platforms and data hosted abroad moved home](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2026/02/20/burkina-faso-zoom-sur-les-12-chantiers-strategiques-du-ministere-de-la-transition-digitale-focus-sur-le-chantier-zero-donnee-a-lexterieur-souverainete-des-donnees-via-des-datacenters-locaux/>), to the two national government datacentres. The ANPTIC portal says the [G-Cloud has 4 datacentres and 8 cloud nodes](<https://www.cloud.gov.bf/>). In the last twelve months, an official said in August 2026 that [over 120 government platforms are hosted abroad and their repatriation has begun](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2026/08/17/transformation-digitale-au-burkina-faso-le-secteur-injecte-142-milliards-de-fcfa-dans-le-plan-relance-pour-une-souverainete-numerique-accrue/>). No source found since October 2023 says a government contract carries terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit. Mature would need a foreign-provider contract with terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or source code.

[Mmegi reports](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/govt-moves-to-in-house-local-data/news>) that Botswana's Data Protection Act, in effect since January 2025, requires a copy of data sent abroad to remain in Botswana. It covers personal data in general, not state data. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the communications minister [said the whole government system is being migrated to a secure government cloud](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/93395>). In April 2026 BoFiNet's chief executive [said government had decided to move its critical services to the Digital Delta Data Centre](<https://businessweekly.co.bw/news/bofinet-pushes-for-local-data-hosting-to-strengthen-security>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule in force covers state data. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

[Paradigm Initiative's Londa 2023 report](<https://paradigmhq.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/CAR-Londa-Report.pdf>), published in 2024, says the Central African Republic has no stand-alone data protection law or regulation. It has none specifically on biometric databases or on data localisation, and no officially recognised national cybersecurity strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says control of state data is a stated goal. Preparing would need a government strategy, plan or draft rule to keep state data or systems under national control.

The Ministry of Digital Transition's 2024 [national data governance strategy SNGD 2030](<https://www.telecom.gouv.ci/new/uploads/publications/174196707541.pdf>) sets a principle for critical information infrastructure. Such data must be processed and stored inside Côte d'Ivoire. In the last twelve months, the digital minister [said in December 2025 that the national data centre at VITIB Grand-Bassam will host the State's strategic data](<https://www.ivoirematin.com/fr/news/Societe/grand-bassam-ibrahim-kalil-konate-met-la-pression-pour-accelerer-le-chantier-du-data-center-national_n_125095.html>). In July 2026 Digital Mag [reported the centre due by the end of 2026](<https://digitalmag.ci/stockage-de-donnees-les-10-datacenters-en-cote-divoire-pour-un-debut-de-souverainete-numerique/>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

At SAGO 2026, [Le Jour reports](<https://lejour.cm/stragie-le-cameroun-mise-sur-la-souverainete-numerique/>), Camtel presented the Tier III Zamengoe data centre it is building. Its aim is to preserve data generated on national territory. In the last twelve months, [CAMTEL said at the SAGO conference of 9 June 2026](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/5885/camtel-highlights-digital-sovereignty-and-data-protection-at-government-action-fair-in-yaounde>) that the centre ensures the security, continuity and local control of government data. Cameroon's personal data protection law imposes local storage requirements. It covers personal data in general, not state data. No source found since October 2023 says a rule in force covers state data. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

A government official is quoted in [the ministry's report of 24 July 2025](<https://sgptntic.gouv.cd/transition-numerique-le-ministre-augustin-kibassa-maliba-visite-le-data-center-du-gouvernement/>). The official says the telecommunications law requires all public administration data to be hosted in the government data centre in Kinshasa. In July 2026 [the Ministry of Social Affairs said the Registre Social Unique is a 100% sovereign system](<https://minas.gouv.cd/registre-social-unique-rsu-un-levier-essentiel-pour-la-protection-sociale-en-rdc/>) with its data hosted nationally. In the last twelve months, on 9 November 2026 the digital development agency named [a sovereign data-hosting space](<https://medd.gouv.cd/nation-digitale-2030-a-kinshasa-les-dsi-de-letat-simposent-comme-les-artisans-de-la-transformation-numerique/>) as a priority. No source found since October 2023 says a government contract carries terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit. Mature would need a foreign-provider contract with such terms.

In June 2026 the UN Economic Commission for Africa [ran workshops](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/eca-supporting-republic-congo-shaping-national-data-governance-strategy-digital-sovereignty-and>) with Congo's digital economy ministry. They worked toward a national data governance strategy. The ministry says the national data centre in Brazzaville [is meant to keep strategic state data](<https://numerique.gouv.cg/actualites/data-center-national>) in the country. In the last twelve months, in February 2026 the African Development Bank's president [said it would open by May 2026](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/congo-le-datacenter-national-operationnel-dici-mai-2026-selon-le-president-de-la-bad/>). In September 2026 Sika Finance reported it would be [delivered by the end of 2026](<https://www.sikafinance.com/marches/congo-le-nouveau-datacenter-national-livre-dici-la-fin-de-l-annee-2026_64496>). No rule in force on state data has been found. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

ANADEN and Comores Câbles [launched the public administration's first data centre on 19 May 2025](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/journ%C3%A9e-mondiale-des-t%C3%A9l%C3%A9communications-i-une-journ%C3%A9e-pour-une-double-c%C3%A9l%C3%A9bration.html>). In the last twelve months, Comoros validated a national data governance strategy at a workshop in Moroni on 24-25 August 2026, [Al-Watwan reports](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/gouvernance-des-donn%C3%A9es-i-les-comores-se-dotent-d%E2%80%99une-strat%C3%A9gie-nationale.html>). Its first axis is data sovereignty, with the State seeking to control the production, storage and use of administration data. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

No stage is set. In February 2026 [Cabo Verde's Secretary of State for the Digital Economy said](<https://www.balai.cv/noticias/atualidade/governo-afirma-que-transicao-energetica-e-condicao-para-a-soberania-digital-de-cabo-verde/>) the State Data Center in Praia, run under NOSi, sustains the state's digital platforms. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says control of state data is a stated goal or a rule in force, and hosting does not answer that. Preparing would need a government strategy, plan or draft rule to keep state data or systems under national control.

No stage is set. The only item found is the [Registre National des Personnes Physiques](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/decret-n2020-146-pr-mi-portant-modalites-dacces-dexploitation-et-de-communication-du-registre-national-des-personnes-physiques/>). Nothing found since October 2023 says whether control of state data is a stated goal or a rule. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying no policy or law governs where state data is held.

[Presidential decree 25-320 of 31 December 2025 sets five levels of data classification, from public to top secret](<https://almostathmir.dz/%D8%AD%D9%88%D9%83%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1-%D8%AA%D8%B9%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%B2-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A7/>). In the last twelve months, [El Watan reported a second data centre planned in Blida](<https://elwatan.dz/tebboune-inaugure-a-mohammadia-le-premier-centre-national-algerien-des-services-numeriques/>) for the national cloud. In October 2026 [L'Echo d'Algérie said the Mohammadia data centre houses the national cloud](<https://lechodalgerie.dz/fibre-optique-en-lalgerie-4-millions-de-foyers-raccordes/>), with administrations' strategic data stored and processed in Algeria. No source found since October 2023 says a government contract carries terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit. Mature would need a foreign-provider contract with terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or source code.

[Digital Policy Alert records](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12346-data-localisation-requirement-in-cloud-first-policy-2024>) that Egypt's Cloud First Policy, adopted on 13 March 2024, entered into force on 22 August 2024. It requires data classified top secret or secret to be hosted within Egypt. President El-Sisi [opened the Government Data and Cloud Computing Center](<https://www.sis.gov.eg/Story/192611/President-El-Sisi-Witnesses-Inauguration-of-Government-Data,-Cloud-Computing-Center?lang=en-us>) on 28 April 2024. In the last twelve months, [on 3 November 2026 the chair of the House ICT committee said the government would submit a bill within weeks](<https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/4400426>) on how data is classified and shared between government sectors. No source found since October 2023 says a government contract carries terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit. Mature would need a foreign-provider contract with terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or source code.

No stage is set. In January 2026 [Eritrea's government received the complete source code of ASYCUDA World with the system](<https://shabait.com/2026/01/08/eritrea-launches-landmark-digital-customs-system>), the Ministry of Information's Shabait reports. [A UN Economic Commission for Africa profile published in 2022](<https://dtri.uneca.org/v1/uploads/country-profile/eri-country-profile-en.pdf>) says Eritrea does not require local data storage. No change in a goal or rule on state data has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since 2023 says control of state data is a stated goal. Preparing would need a government strategy, plan or draft rule to keep state data or systems under national control.

[Digital Policy Alert records](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12100-data-localisation-requirements-in-personal-data-protection-proclamation-proclamation-no-13212024>) that Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 entered into force on 24 July 2024. It requires locally collected personal data to be stored on servers in Ethiopia, and covers personal data in general, not state data. In the last twelve months, the innovation ministry [said in December 2025 that the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy rests on a sovereign national cloud](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_8021907>). In November 2026 the minister [ordered faster work on the National Cloud Data Center](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/8212/x>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule in force covers state data. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

On 3 July 2026 Gabon's President [inaugurated the Nkok national data centre](<https://depeches241.com/?p=29457>). It is meant to bring hosting of strategic state data back to Gabon. In the last twelve months, the Minister of Digital Economy [announced on 9 June 2026 that the first national data centre would open on 30 June 2026](<https://www.gabonreview.com/hebergement-des-donnees-le-gabon-met-fin-a-sa-dependance-aux-serveurs-etrangers-avec-son-premier-datacenter/>). In November 2025 AGP reported that [the La Poste data centre hosts critical public administration services](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-transformation-numerique-paule-marie-gondjout-et-mark-alexandre-doumba-en-visite-au-data-center-de-la-poste/>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

[Communications Minister Sam George said at the ACR2 opening](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/digital-realty-opens-ghanas-largest-data-center-in-accra.html>) that Ghana has a localisation policy. Local data processed on clouds outside the country will have to be hosted in Ghana. A [bidding document](<https://moc.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Final-Bidding_Document_for_Data_Center_Upgrade.pdf>) says NITA runs two national data centres, in Accra and Kumasi. In the last twelve months, in November 2026 the minister said [G-Cloud, Ghana's national cloud platform, gives government institutions secure local hosting](<https://thevaultznews.com/2026/11/02/sensitive-data-must-be-hosted-on-secure-infrastructure-sam-george/>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule in force covers state data. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

Guinea [launched its national Data Center on 4 September 2025](<https://guineenews.org/2025/09/04/guinee-le-ministre-djiba-diakite-procede-au-double-lancement-du-point-gn-et-le-data-center-national-tier-lll/>), a Tier III site, and the telecommunications minister said the country's strategic data now stays in Guinea. On 31 July 2025 Enabel [handed the territorial administration ministry the source code of the civil registration database](<https://planete7.info/modernisation-de-letat-civil-en-guinee-enabel-remet-un-important-lot-de-materiel-informatique-aux-autorites-guineennes/>). In the last twelve months, an [AI roadmap](<https://guineematin.com/2025/12/20/intelligence-artificielle-guinee-rapport-national-feuille-de-route/>) presented on 19 December 2025 proposed a national data hub and a sovereign cloud. No rule in force on where state data is held was found. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

No stage is set. The only item found is the [Government Cloud (G-Cloud)](<https://policies.gov.gm/d/b007fc10-80d2-11ef-b086-029254d29bb1>). Nothing found since October 2023 says whether control of state data is a stated goal or a rule. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying no policy or law governs where state data is held.

[Implementation guidelines of the 2025 Kenya Cloud Policy](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/corporate/technology/search-for-firm-to-host-sensitive-state-data-on-cloud-begins-5549208>) require top secret State data to be held in a data centre within Kenya. [The Konza National Data Centre](<https://pppkenya.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Updated-ADDENDUM-III-TRANSACTION-ADVISORY-SERVICES-FOR-THE-KONZA-CLOUD-EXPANSION-AND-SAMRT-CITY-FACILITIES.pdf>) hosts 145 of Kenya's 451 government institutions. In the last twelve months, the PPP Directorate [signed a funding agreement in October 2026](<https://pppkenya.go.ke/ppp-directorate-signs-funding-agreement-for-konza-national-data-centre-cloud-expansion/>) for the Konza cloud expansion. No source found since October 2023 says a government contract carries terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit. Mature would need a foreign-provider contract with terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or source code.

In August 2026 Andrew Peters, head of the National Identification Registry, [told a press conference that all data of the national ID scheme will be stored within Liberia](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202611/revenue-sharing-data-sovereignty-concerns-arise-from-liberia-id-card-concession>). The pledge covers the ID scheme alone. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 he [said the signed US$54.7 million concession leaves the identity data with the state](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberia-nir-us54-7m-digital-id-deal-awaits-legislative-approval/>). It awaits the legislature's approval. No law, decree or policy setting where state data must be held has been found. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

Libya's Cabinet Decision 358 of 2026 [set up an authority](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%d9%82%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%b1-%d9%85%d8%ac%d9%84%d8%b3-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%88%d8%b2%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%a1-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-358-%d9%84%d8%b3%d9%86%d8%a9-2026-%d9%85-%d8%a8%d8%b4%d8%a3%d9%86-%d8%a5%d9%86%d8%b4/>) to prepare national digital sovereignty policies, classify national data and regulate the hosting of national data. In the last twelve months, the Central Bank of Libya's Circular No. 18 [prohibited storing personal, financial, credit or sensitive data outside Libya](<https://informatics.ly/en/session/personal-data-protection-regulation-session/>) from 1 July 2026. It binds banks and payment firms, not state bodies. No source found since October 2023 says a rule in force covers state data. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

Article 11 of Morocco's 2020 cybersecurity law, loi n° 05-20, [requires sensitive data to be hosted only on national territory](<https://www.anrt.ma/sites/default/files/2022-02/loi_05-20_cybersecurite_fr.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the draft 2027 finance bill went to Parliament on 23 October 2026. It [provides for the Jazari-Root sovereign data centre in Rabat](<https://lhybride.ma/briefs/plf-2027-cloud-first-ministere-ia/>) for the state's strategic data. In June 2026 Le Brief reported that the social support agency's systems [are hosted in the finance ministry's data centre](<https://www.lebrief.ma/soutien-social-un-an-apres-impact-de-lanss-100155241/>). No source found since 2023 says a rule in force covers state data. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

In January 2026 Madagascar's digital minister [named a sovereign national data centre for public data](<https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202601200231.html>) among the ministry's priorities. Eu SEE reports that draft Bill 40 of 2026 [defines digital sovereignty](<https://eusee.hivos.org/alert/postponement-of-vote-on-cybercrime-and-digital-communications-bills-which-raise-online-civic-space-concerns/>) as state surveillance and control of critical data and infrastructure. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the National Assembly [postponed the vote](<https://eusee.hivos.org/alert/postponement-of-vote-on-cybercrime-and-digital-communications-bills-which-raise-online-civic-space-concerns/>) on the bill. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

On 13 February 2024 [the government presented Mali Kura Biométrie](<https://bamada.net/donnees-administratives-le-mali-recupere-ses-fichiers-ravec>) as a sovereign system keeping the RAVEC identity data under national control. The president called it the starting point of Mali's digital sovereignty. In 2022 [ITU stated](<https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-d/opb/pref/D-PREF-THEM.29-2022-PDF-F.pdf>) that AGETIC, a government agency, runs a data centre for the public administration. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

[The UNECA/GIZ/AU inception report says](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/sites/default/files/resources/documents/TICID/data-governance-framework-mozambique/en_project_inception_report_mozambique_data_governance_framework.pdf>) that Banco de Moçambique Notice 4/GGBM/2003 requires data centres to be located in Mozambique. It covers banks, not state data. INTIC's draft [Regulamento dos Servicos de Computacao em Nuvem](<https://intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/INTIC-Regulamento-dos-Provedores-de-Servic%CC%A7os-de-Computac%CC%A7a%CC%83o-em-Nuvem-23-12-2024-versa%CC%83o-consulta-pu%CC%81blica-1.pdf>) went to public consultation on 24 February 2025. Its Art. 11(2) keeps classified information in national territory unless the regulator expressly authorises otherwise. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

On 29 June 2026 Mauritania [launched its national cloud at the National Data Center in Nouakchott](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/3006-56943-mauritania-launches-national-cloud-to-strengthen-digital-sovereignty>), Ecofin Agency reports. It hosts government data and digital public services in the country. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 the digital minister [told the National Assembly that all government servers had been moved into a data centre the ministry built](<https://www.ami.mr/archives/263232>). No source found since October 2023 says a law, decree or policy in force classifies government data. None says one requires it to be held in the country. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

In September 2025 the ICT ministry [issued a request for information for a sovereign cloud for the government](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Bidding-Document-RFI-for-Sovereign-Cloud-for-the-Government-of-Mauritius.docx>). It would run under Mauritian law in a local data centre. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the Cabinet [discussed a National Sovereign Cloud](<https://ionnews.mu/maurice-veut-lancer-un-national-sovereign-cloud-pour-proteger-ses-donnees/>). In November 2026 CERT-MU's director [said the government keeps its data on its own cloud in Mauritius](<https://defimedia.info/apres-la-panne-de-microsoft-365-la-dependance-numerique-un-risque-pour-maurice>). No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

In 2022 [the UN Economic Commission for Africa's profile of Malawi](<https://www.uneca.org/sites/default/files/ATPC/cp/Digital%20trade%20regulatory%20integration%20-%20Country%20profile%20-%20Malawi-%20ENG.pdf>) stated that Malawi has local storage requirements only for health-related data. It named no instrument. [A request for bids says](<https://api.pppc.mw/api/download/722>) the Department of e-Government runs the National Data Centre in Lilongwe, which hosts systems of ministries, departments and agencies. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 the department sought bids to expand the centre. No source found since October 2023 says a law, decree or policy in force classifies government data or requires it to be held in the country. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

In August 2025 Namibia's sixth national development plan, [NDP6, planned a National Data Centre](<https://neweralive.na/namibia-targets-full-digital-transformation/>) to keep government data in the country. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the Prime Minister's spokesperson said [the centre was at a preliminary stage, with nothing procured](<https://theissue.com.na/namibia-wallows-in-digital-sovereignty-illusion/>). In July 2026 the head of 6th Grain, a US firm, [spoke of its agriculture ministry contract](<https://theissue.com.na/govt-probes-n40m-us-agriculture-deal/>). He said all its code passes to the government on completion. No source found says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

In July 2025 Niger [installed a national committee to oversee critical digital infrastructure](<https://westafricaweekly.com/niger-sets-up-national-committee-to-oversee-critical-digital-infrastructure-in-response-to-rising-cyber-threats/>). In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the government [mentioned plans to enhance its national data center capacity](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202603/focus-on-sahel-digital-sovereignty>).
